title: Use support runbooks: map expected errors to diagnostic and resolution steps
summary: Use the support runbook that matches the expected error/fatal category you are investigating, then follow its prescribed diagnostic steps and resolution steps. If the observed error/fatal does not fit any expected error type in the runbook, use the support handoff approach: consult RCA documentation in Confluence and then resolve (optionally updating the RCA with new information).
when_to_use: When you are investigating an observed error/fatal and need a support-oriented path that maps the error category to (1) expected error types, (2) steps to diagnose, and (3) steps to resolve.
not_for: Do not proceed with runbook steps if the observed error/fatal does not match any expected error type in the runbook; instead use the RCA/Confluence handoff approach described in the source.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Select the runbook that corresponds to the error/fatal type being investigated; follow the runbook’s steps to diagnose and steps to resolve for the matching expected error category.
Support handoff person (as described by the source): Acts as the handoff point during support engagement and helps drive the RCA/Confluence-based resolution workflow.
access_or_tools_needed: Support runbook documentation (as referenced by the source)
Confluence (for RCA documentation, as referenced by the source)

external_references: Confluence RCA documentation (consult as described in the source)

visual_references.description: Frame showing the source description of runbooks as support-oriented (expected errors, steps to diagnose, steps to resolve) and the handoff approach using RCA in Confluence.

steps.title: Open the support runbook that corresponds to the error/fatal type you are investigating
steps.purpose: Start from the correct support-oriented runbook so you can map the observed error/fatal to the runbook’s expected error category.
steps.instruction: Open the support runbook that corresponds to the error/fatal type you are investigating.
steps.expected_result: You have the relevant runbook open that contains a section listing the “types of errors expected” and associated diagnostic and resolution steps.
steps.healthy_condition: The runbook you opened includes an expected-error categorization section and provides steps to diagnose and steps to resolve for those categories.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find a runbook that contains the expected-error categories for the error/fatal you are investigating.

actions.label: Open matching runbook
actions.exact_action: Open the runbook that corresponds to the error/fatal type you are investigating

steps.title: Identify the “types of errors expected” section and confirm the observed error/fatal matches an expected error category
steps.purpose: Ensure you follow the diagnostic and resolution steps for the correct expected error category.
steps.instruction: In the opened runbook, locate the section that lists the “types of errors expected” and confirm your observed error/fatal matches one of the expected error categories.
steps.expected_result: Your observed error/fatal is mapped to a specific expected error category listed in the runbook’s “types of errors expected” section.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed error/fatal aligns with one of the expected error categories in the runbook.
steps.failure_condition: The observed error/fatal does not match any expected error type/category in the runbook.

actions.label: Check expected error category
actions.exact_action: Identify the “types of errors expected” section in the runbook and confirm your observed error/fatal matches the expected error category

steps.purpose: Perform the runbook-prescribed diagnosis steps that correspond to the expected error category you mapped in the previous step.
steps.instruction: Follow the runbook’s “steps to diagnose” for the expected error type/category that matches your observed error/fatal.
steps.expected_result: You complete the runbook’s diagnostic steps associated with the mapped expected error category.
steps.healthy_condition: The diagnostic steps you are executing are the ones explicitly associated with the mapped expected error category in the runbook.

actions.label: Execute diagnose steps

steps.title: Follow the runbook’s “steps to resolve” for the matching expected error type
steps.purpose: Apply the runbook-prescribed resolution steps for the expected error category that matches your observed error/fatal.
steps.instruction: Follow the runbook’s “steps to resolve” for that expected error type/category.
steps.expected_result: You complete the runbook’s resolution steps associated with the mapped expected error category.
steps.healthy_condition: The resolution steps you are executing are the ones explicitly associated with the mapped expected error category in the runbook.
steps.failure_condition: You are executing resolution steps that do not correspond to the mapped expected error category.

actions.label: Execute resolve steps

steps.title: If the runbook is incomplete or the error/fatal does not match, use the RCA/Confluence handoff approach and then resolve (optionally update RCA)
steps.purpose: Provide a fallback resolution path when the runbook does not cover the observed error/fatal category.
steps.instruction: If the runbook information is incomplete or the observed error/fatal does not match any expected error type in the runbook, use the source-described support handoff approach: consult RCA documentation in Confluence and then resolve; optionally update RCA with new information.
steps.expected_result: You consult RCA in Confluence and use it to drive resolution; if new information is discovered, you update the RCA as described by the source.
steps.healthy_condition: Resolution is driven by RCA documentation in Confluence when the runbook mapping fails or is incomplete.
steps.failure_condition: You continue using runbook steps despite the observed error/fatal not matching any expected error type in the runbook.

actions.label: Consult RCA in Confluence

success_criteria: Observed error/fatal is mapped to a runbook expected error category (when a match exists).
Diagnostic steps and resolution steps executed correspond to the mapped expected error category in the runbook.
If no match exists or runbook info is incomplete, RCA in Confluence is consulted and used to drive resolution (with optional RCA updates).
healthy_conditions: Runbook contains expected error categories plus steps to diagnose and steps to resolve.
You follow the runbook sections that correspond to the mapped expected error category.
When runbook mapping fails, RCA in Confluence is used as the resolution knowledge source.
failure_conditions: Observed error/fatal does not match any expected error type in the runbook and you do not switch to the RCA/Confluence handoff approach.
You execute diagnose/resolve steps that do not correspond to the mapped expected error category.
escalation_guidance: If the observed error/fatal does not match any expected error type in the runbook, stop and use the RCA/Confluence handoff process described in the source (consult RCA in Confluence, then resolve; optionally update RCA).
